scope: Browser-local structural parsing of the United States reporter citation forms explicitly recognized by rule version 1.0.0.
prohibitedInference: A passing structural result does not establish that an authority exists, remains good law, is quoted accurately, or supports a proposition.

cases.input: Brown v. Board of Education, 347 U.S. 483 (1954).
The court cited 410 F.3d 25 (2005); the point remains disputed.
This sentence contains no reporter citation.
2024 WL 123456 is a database identifier outside rule 1.0.0.
Section 1983 is a statutory reference, not a supported reporter citation.
This invented proposition cites a structurally plausible 347 U.S. 483 (1954).

knownLimitations: The corpus is synthetic and tests deterministic structural behavior, not real-world source retrieval.
The supported reporter grammar is intentionally narrow and omits statutes, regulations, docket citations, database identifiers, slip opinions, state reporters, and many parallel-citation forms.
A structurally plausible citation can be fabricated or attached to a false proposition; CV-020 is required to remain unflagged to demonstrate that boundary.
The public parser does not retrieve authority, run citator treatment, compare quotations, or evaluate proposition support.
retestTrigger: Any parser, reporter allow-list, regular expression, result taxonomy, browser runtime, or public capability claim change; otherwise 2026-10-31.
